evals.prompt: We have an approved 10-task implementation plan in docs/plans/feature.md. How should the orchestrator execute it without burning main session tokens?
evals.expected_output: Execute using Subagent-Driven Development (SDD): resolve the plan workspace via sdd_workspace.py, generate task briefs via task_brief.py, and dispatch a fresh worker per task on a cheap model tier. Verify each task with an independent review package before proceeding. Do not poll status in a loop; call wait and yield.

evals.prompt: What is the difference between TDD and SDD, and how do they work together?
evals.expected_output: TDD is a micro-level coding technique (RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR) governing how code is written inside a task. SDD is a macro-level workflow governing how the orchestrator manages multi-task plans, isolates context across workers, and enforces review gates. SDD mandates that implementer subagents follow TDD inside their briefs.

evals.prompt: Why should an orchestrator avoid polling get_agent_status in a loop after dispatching a subagent?
evals.expected_output: Polling in a loop repeatedly re-sends the growing conversation context to the model on every turn, burning hundreds of thousands to millions of tokens unnecessarily. The orchestrator must call wait once and yield control; the host runtime notifies it upon subagent completion.
